_**User**_

We are now entering the IMPLEMENTATION phase of the Support Ticket Management System.

This is NOT a request to blindly build the complete application.

The project follows:

Requirements
→ Requirements Decisions
→ Architecture
→ Data Model
→ API Contract
→ State Machine
→ UI Flow
→ Implementation
→ Testing
→ Review
→ Fix

SOURCE OF TRUTH

Before changing anything, read:

- spec/architecture.md
- spec/data-model.md
- spec/api-contract.md
- spec/state-machine.md
- spec/ui-flow.md
- .cursor/rules/

Also inspect the current repository before creating files.

Do not invent product requirements that are not present in these specifications.

==================================================
IMPLEMENTATION SCOPE
==================================================

For this session implement:

1. Project/runtime foundation
2. Backend domain model
3. Persistence/database foundation
4. State-machine implementation
5. Backend/domain tests
6. Local development/run configuration
7. Basic frontend scaffold

Do NOT implement the complete REST API or complete frontend ticket UI yet.

==================================================
1. PROJECT STRUCTURE
==================================================

Create:

backend/
frontend/

Backend:
- Java 21
- Spring Boot
- Maven
- Spring Web
- Spring Data JPA
- PostgreSQL
- H2 for tests
- Jakarta Validation
- Flyway
- Spring Boot testing

Frontend:
- React
- Vite
- TypeScript

Backend and frontend must be independently runnable.

==================================================
2. LOCAL PORTS
==================================================

Do NOT use the default ports such as:

8080
3000

Use the 8000-series.

Use:

Backend:
http://localhost:8000

Frontend:
http://localhost:8001

Configure Spring Boot accordingly.

Configure Vite accordingly.

If the frontend needs to communicate with the backend during development, configure the Vite development proxy to forward API requests to:

http://localhost:8000

Do not hard-code production secrets.

Document these ports clearly.

==================================================
3. LOCAL DEVELOPMENT DOCUMENTATION
==================================================

Create/update README.md with a clear:

"Run Locally"

section.

It must explain step-by-step:

Prerequisites:
- Java 21
- Maven
- Node.js/npm
- PostgreSQL

How to configure PostgreSQL locally.

Explain the required environment/configuration values without committing real passwords.

Explain how to start the backend.

Explain how to start the frontend.

Example structure:

Terminal 1:
cd backend
mvn spring-boot:run

Backend:
http://localhost:8000

Terminal 2:
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev

Frontend:
http://localhost:8001

Also document:

- how to run backend tests
- how to build backend
- how to build frontend
- where the API will be available
- where the UI will be available
- which database the application uses
- how Flyway migrations are applied
- how H2 is used during tests

Do not claim a command works unless you verify it.

==================================================
4. BACKEND DOMAIN MODEL
==================================================

Implement the data model from:

spec/data-model.md

Ticket:

- UUID id
- title
- description
- priority
- assignee
- status
- created timestamp
- updated timestamp

Comment:

- UUID id
- ticket relationship
- body
- created timestamp

Enums:

TicketStatus:
OPEN
IN_PROGRESS
RESOLVED
CLOSED
CANCELLED

Priority:
LOW
MEDIUM
HIGH

New tickets always start with:

OPEN

The client must not control the initial status.

Do not create a User entity.

==================================================
5. STATE MACHINE
==================================================

Implement the state machine from:

spec/state-machine.md

ONLY these transitions are allowed:

OPEN -> IN_PROGRESS
IN_PROGRESS -> RESOLVED
RESOLVED -> CLOSED
OPEN -> CANCELLED
IN_PROGRESS -> CANCELLED

Every other transition is invalid.

Same-status transitions are also invalid.

The backend/domain layer owns this rule.

Do not put the state machine in:
- controllers
- repositories
- frontend

Use a meaningful domain exception for invalid transitions.

==================================================
6. DATABASE
==================================================

Use:

Application:
PostgreSQL

Tests:
H2 where practical

Use Spring Data JPA.

Use Flyway migrations for the application schema.

Minimal tables:

ticket
comment

Requirements:

- UUID primary keys
- comment foreign key to ticket
- nullable assignee
- persisted status
- persisted priority
- persisted timestamps
- appropriate constraints

Do not add unnecessary tables or features.

==================================================
7. VALIDATION
==================================================

Implement only agreed validation:

Ticket:
- title non-blank
- description non-blank
- priority LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH
- assignee optional

Comment:
- body non-blank

Do not invent arbitrary maximum lengths or additional business rules.

==================================================
8. TESTING
==================================================

Create tests for the state machine.

Test all five valid transitions.

Test representative and complete invalid transitions according to the agreed closed matrix.

At minimum verify:

OPEN -> OPEN ❌
OPEN -> RESOLVED ❌
OPEN -> CLOSED ❌
IN_PROGRESS -> OPEN ❌
IN_PROGRESS -> CLOSED ❌
RESOLVED -> OPEN ❌
RESOLVED -> IN_PROGRESS ❌
RESOLVED -> CANCELLED ❌
CLOSED -> OPEN ❌
CANCELLED -> OPEN ❌

Also test same-status transitions for every status.

Verify that ticket creation results in OPEN.

Tests must test behaviour rather than implementation details.

==================================================
9. FRONTEND FOUNDATION
==================================================

Create only the basic React/Vite/TypeScript scaffold.

Configure:

Frontend port:
8001

Backend:
8000

Configure the Vite proxy so future API requests can use the backend without hard-coding the backend URL throughout the UI.

Do NOT build ticket screens yet.

==================================================
10. SECURITY / SECRETS
==================================================

Do not commit:

- database passwords
- API keys
- .env files containing secrets
- credentials

Add appropriate entries to .gitignore.

Use environment/configuration placeholders.

==================================================
11. VERIFICATION
==================================================

After implementation:

1. Run backend tests.
2. Run backend build.
3. Run frontend dependency installation if required.
4. Run frontend build.
5. Start backend locally and verify it starts on port 8000.
6. Start frontend locally and verify it starts on port 8001.
7. Verify the frontend can reach the backend through the configured development proxy if applicable.
8. Fix genuine implementation/setup problems.

Do not change specifications simply to make the build pass.
